title: Aft Lower Shell Skin Panel — External Repair Patch on the Lower Shell
abstract: Permanent repair for impact or corrosion damage to the aft lower shell skin, installing an external patch over the damaged bay with a two-row fastener pattern and a continuous sealing bead.

sections.purpose: To give the permanent repair for damage to the aft lower shell skin panel that exceeds the blend-out limits, by installing an external repair patch over the affected bay.
sections.damage_assessment: Damage to the aft lower shell is most often impact from ground equipment at the belly fairing edge or corrosion under a repair that has lost its sealing. Assess the damage with the bay opened from inside and the paint removed over the affected area from outside. Measure the maximum dimension in the fore and aft direction and across, and record the distance to the nearest frame, stringer and existing repair. An area that already carries a repair patch cannot take a second patch over it; the existing patch must be removed and the assessment redone against the parent skin. Do an eddy current inspection of the whole bay before deciding the repair, because impact damage at the belly fairing edge often has a second indication at the opposite corner of the bay.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the belly fairing panel and get access to the bay from inside. Remove the paint over the damaged area and for 100 mm beyond. Cut out the damaged material to the envelope on the drawing, keeping the corner radii at the minimum on the drawing and deburring every edge. Do an eddy current inspection around the whole cut-out. Cut the patch from the skin panel material and form it to the local curvature on the forming block. Position the patch so that it gives at least 25 mm edge distance to the cut-out and clears every frame and stringer land by 15 mm. Drill the two-row pattern through the patch into the parent skin using the drill jig. Do an eddy current inspection at every new hole before any fastener is installed. Deburr and clean both faces. Apply the surface treatment to the faying faces and let it stand. Install the patch D5331121169495 wet with sealant, with the joint angle D5331122892194 at the aft edge where the drawing requires it, and fasten with rivets EN545167-02. Install washers AGS334024-84 at the drain positions and check that the drain path is clear with a water flow test. Apply the continuous sealing bead around the patch perimeter and tool it to the profile on the drawing. Re-apply the paint scheme.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do an eddy current inspection around the patch perimeter at completion and record the baseline. Repeat the eddy current inspection at every second heavy check. Do a detailed visual inspection of the sealing bead at every heavy check and re-seal any lifting before it admits moisture. A patch that shows any indication at the perimeter must be referred to the engineering department; the patch may not be enlarged in service.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Cut-out up to 180 mm in the fore and aft direction and 120 mm across, confined to one bay, no closer than 40 mm to a frame or stringer land, and not overlapping an existing repair.

repair_drawings.title: External repair patch and fastener pattern, aft lower shell bay

type_data.fastener_pattern: Two rows, 96 rivets total, 20 mm pitch, 25 mm edge distance to the cut-out and 15 mm minimum clearance to any frame or stringer land.
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Repair is life-limited to 24 000 flight cycles with a repeat eddy current inspection of the perimeter every 8 000 flight cycles. The patch may not be enlarged in service.
